newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares rise, focus remains on banks.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares rise, focus remains on banks.

text.p: Norwegian shares climbed almost three percent on Monday gaining impetus from overseas markets and from a rebound in offshore and technology stocks.
Oslo's Total index advanced 2.75 percent at 1,063.34 points in mediocre turnover of 829 million crowns.

Brokers said the market was riding on the tails of European bourse following the pre-weekend rebound on Wall Street. There had been no change in domestic factors and investors would continue to watch the U.S. market and interest rates, they said.
Banks remained under focus after last week's merger proposal between Storebrand and Christiania Bank.

Mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank), itself at the centre of a bidding standoff between Fokus Bank and Den norske Bank (DnB), was the second most traded share in value-terms at 80.2 million crowns. The stock had advanced two percent to 209 crowns.
DnB said on Monday it had acquired the option to buy a further 622,000 shares in BNbank, bring its total shareholding to 15.2 percent.
The most traded share was Norsk Hydro, which gained 11.50 crowns to 328.50 crowns in turnover of 93.7 million crowns. --Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41
